programme.desc: Sometimes we get a bit stuck in the past with heritage homes, fixating on the original build year and forget that the home and society has evolved over 140 years. programme.title: The Inspire Action Podcast
programme.desc:
What does it mean to be part of nature, not apart from it? And how can an ancient philosophy guide us toward practical, systemic change in the modern world?
In this episode of the Inspire Action Podcast Ciara sits down with Dr. Simon Sadinsky - professor, Executive Director of Education, and in-house Harmony advisor at the Kings Foundation - to explore a philosophy that has guided cultures and peoples around the world for millennia, but is now finally being integrated into Western thought via a few key changemakers along the way. It shouldn’t be revolutionary, but it is in our world where progress often comes at the cost of the natural world around us.
Simon reminds us that Harmony isn't just philosophy - it's a practical roadmap for action. This conversation will hopefully shift how you see your place in the world, and remind you (as it did for us) that we all have a part to play in creating the Harmony our planet so desperately needs.
programme.sub-title: How Can We Reconnect with Nature? with Dr. Simon Sadinsky

programme.desc:
What does it mean to be part of nature, not apart from it? And how can an ancient philosophy guide us toward practical, systemic change in the modern world?
In this episode of the Inspire Action Podcast Ciara sits down with Dr. Simon Sadinsky - professor, Executive Director of Education, and in-house Harmony advisor at the Kings Foundation - to explore a philosophy that has guided cultures and peoples around the world for millennia, but is now finally being integrated into Western thought via a few key changemakers along the way. It shouldn’t be revolutionary, but it is in our world where progress often comes at the cost of the natural world around us.
Simon reminds us that Harmony isn't just philosophy - it's a practical roadmap for action. This conversation will hopefully shift how you see your place in the world, and remind you (as it did for us) that we all have a part to play in creating the Harmony our planet so desperately needs.

programme.title: Bold Backyards
programme.desc: This DIY raised planter is fully made out of cinder blocks! These blocks are staked and then filled with dirt and rock. Traditionally you would pour a concrete footing and then stack the block; I wanted to see if it would work with rock and block adhesive. I love how it turned out, and it's doing amazing so far. If I were in a more wet area, I would have installed a drain, we are in a pretty dry area, and this dirt is mostly granite, clay, and rock. I have found there isn't much settling that occurs in this area.

programme.title: The Inspire Action Podcast
programme.desc:
What does it mean to be part of nature, not apart from it? And how can an ancient philosophy guide us toward practical, systemic change in the modern world?
In this episode of the Inspire Action Podcast Ciara sits down with Dr. Simon Sadinsky - professor, Executive Director of Education, and in-house Harmony advisor at the Kings Foundation - to explore a philosophy that has guided cultures and peoples around the world for millennia, but is now finally being integrated into Western thought via a few key changemakers along the way. It shouldn’t be revolutionary, but it is in our world where progress often comes at the cost of the natural world around us.
Simon reminds us that Harmony isn't just philosophy - it's a practical roadmap for action. This conversation will hopefully shift how you see your place in the world, and remind you (as it did for us) that we all have a part to play in creating the Harmony our planet so desperately needs.
programme.sub-title: How Can We Reconnect with Nature? with Dr. Simon Sadinsky

programme.title: Ideas For Your Home
programme.desc: If you have pets or delicate plantings, it's essential to install deer fencing on your property to keep deer and other animals away. But most often, fence installers place these in unsightly locations. programme.title: Rise: Sustainable Home Tours
programme.desc: Meet Melissa and Jim - they built their dream home a few years ago, but this wasn’t like any other home. Their main goal was to have a healthy home for their kids, and one that would also save on energy and environmental resources.

programme.title: Rise: Sustainable Home Tours

programme.title: Rise: Sustainable Home Tours
programme.desc: Passive House is an easy to understand building standard that takes home energy efficiency to a whole new level using 5 building standards that are explained in this video.

programme.title: Rise: Sustainable Home Tours

programme.desc: Richard & Alix were looking to remodel the home that they raised their children in, and didn't know where to start. Alix is a watercolor artist and had a painting that she wanted in incorporate into the design of the remodel.

programme.title: The Inspire Action Podcast
programme.desc:
What does it mean to be part of nature, not apart from it? And how can an ancient philosophy guide us toward practical, systemic change in the modern world?
In this episode of the Inspire Action Podcast Ciara sits down with Dr. Simon Sadinsky - professor, Executive Director of Education, and in-house Harmony advisor at the Kings Foundation - to explore a philosophy that has guided cultures and peoples around the world for millennia, but is now finally being integrated into Western thought via a few key changemakers along the way. It shouldn’t be revolutionary, but it is in our world where progress often comes at the cost of the natural world around us.
Simon reminds us that Harmony isn't just philosophy - it's a practical roadmap for action. This conversation will hopefully shift how you see your place in the world, and remind you (as it did for us) that we all have a part to play in creating the Harmony our planet so desperately needs.
programme.sub-title: How Can We Reconnect with Nature? with Dr. Simon Sadinsky

programme.title: The Inspire Action Podcast
programme.desc:
What does it mean to be part of nature, not apart from it? And how can an ancient philosophy guide us toward practical, systemic change in the modern world?
In this episode of the Inspire Action Podcast Ciara sits down with Dr. Simon Sadinsky - professor, Executive Director of Education, and in-house Harmony advisor at the Kings Foundation - to explore a philosophy that has guided cultures and peoples around the world for millennia, but is now finally being integrated into Western thought via a few key changemakers along the way. It shouldn’t be revolutionary, but it is in our world where progress often comes at the cost of the natural world around us.
Simon reminds us that Harmony isn't just philosophy - it's a practical roadmap for action. This conversation will hopefully shift how you see your place in the world, and remind you (as it did for us) that we all have a part to play in creating the Harmony our planet so desperately needs.
programme.sub-title: How Can We Reconnect with Nature? with Dr. Simon Sadinsky

programme.title: The Inspire Action Podcast
programme.desc:
What does it mean to be part of nature, not apart from it? And how can an ancient philosophy guide us toward practical, systemic change in the modern world?
In this episode of the Inspire Action Podcast Ciara sits down with Dr. Simon Sadinsky - professor, Executive Director of Education, and in-house Harmony advisor at the Kings Foundation - to explore a philosophy that has guided cultures and peoples around the world for millennia, but is now finally being integrated into Western thought via a few key changemakers along the way. It shouldn’t be revolutionary, but it is in our world where progress often comes at the cost of the natural world around us.
Simon reminds us that Harmony isn't just philosophy - it's a practical roadmap for action. This conversation will hopefully shift how you see your place in the world, and remind you (as it did for us) that we all have a part to play in creating the Harmony our planet so desperately needs.
programme.sub-title: How Can We Reconnect with Nature? with Dr. Simon Sadinsky

programme.title: The Inspire Action Podcast
programme.desc:
What does it mean to be part of nature, not apart from it? And how can an ancient philosophy guide us toward practical, systemic change in the modern world?
In this episode of the Inspire Action Podcast Ciara sits down with Dr. Simon Sadinsky - professor, Executive Director of Education, and in-house Harmony advisor at the Kings Foundation - to explore a philosophy that has guided cultures and peoples around the world for millennia, but is now finally being integrated into Western thought via a few key changemakers along the way. It shouldn’t be revolutionary, but it is in our world where progress often comes at the cost of the natural world around us.
Simon reminds us that Harmony isn't just philosophy - it's a practical roadmap for action. This conversation will hopefully shift how you see your place in the world, and remind you (as it did for us) that we all have a part to play in creating the Harmony our planet so desperately needs.
programme.sub-title: How Can We Reconnect with Nature? with Dr. Simon Sadinsky

programme.title: The Inspire Action Podcast
programme.desc:
What does it mean to be part of nature, not apart from it? And how can an ancient philosophy guide us toward practical, systemic change in the modern world?
In this episode of the Inspire Action Podcast Ciara sits down with Dr. Simon Sadinsky - professor, Executive Director of Education, and in-house Harmony advisor at the Kings Foundation - to explore a philosophy that has guided cultures and peoples around the world for millennia, but is now finally being integrated into Western thought via a few key changemakers along the way. It shouldn’t be revolutionary, but it is in our world where progress often comes at the cost of the natural world around us.
Simon reminds us that Harmony isn't just philosophy - it's a practical roadmap for action. This conversation will hopefully shift how you see your place in the world, and remind you (as it did for us) that we all have a part to play in creating the Harmony our planet so desperately needs.
programme.sub-title: How Can We Reconnect with Nature? with Dr. Simon Sadinsky

programme.sub-title: An Architect-Designed Beach House That Frames Its Ocean Views

programme.title: Landscape Design
programme.desc: Free ad-supported linear TV for the home design & sustainable living audience. Modern interiors, eco landscaping, smart home, outdoor living, and eco travel.
programme.sub-title: Living Walls by TruVine Design | Delray Beach, Florida

programme.title: Simple Dwelling
programme.desc: Architect Douglas Wan wanted something simple for his own tiny apartment, avoiding the fancy gadgetry often found in tiny homes. He thought about how he might want to live in the apartment, with the idea of living a monastic life but in the city.
programme.sub-title: A Minimalist Interior That Gives a Lesson in Tiny Apartment Design

programme.title: Ashley Renne: Sustainable Home
programme.desc: Regrowing scallion from kitchen scraps is one of the easiest DIY zero waste food experiments you can try! Here's how to regrow and harvest your scallions or green onions FAST instead of throwing the scraps away.
programme.sub-title: How To Regrow Scallions From Scraps - Zero Waste Food Tutorial + Harvest

programme.title: Simple Dwelling

programme.title: Landscape Design
programme.desc: A look at 2 different designs by Divine Nature Landscape Design in Los Altos, California. Johnna Brooks of Divine Nature specializes in creating lush gardens that flow.
programme.sub-title: Hillside Restoration by Divine Nature Landscape | Los Gatos, California

programme.title: Ideas For Your Home
programme.desc: It's fall and there are mountains of leaves around our yards. But this abundance of leaves can be put to great use around the landscape. Consider shredding your leaves to create a nutrient-rich ground cover for your yard and planting beds.

programme.title: Ashley Renne: Sustainable Travel
programme.desc: On World Environment Day 2019, history was made -- and Ashley Renne got a chance to be apart of it. The United Airlines "Flight For The Planet" crew flew Ashley and other passengers from Chicago to Los Angeles on the most Eco-Friendly flight in aviation history.
programme.sub-title: Ep 3 - Is This The Most Eco-friendly Flight In History | Biofuel + Zero Waste

programme.title: Ashley Renne: Sustainable Travel
programme.desc: In this first episode, Ashley explores sustainability in Thailand; She arrives in Phuket and takes a speedboat to the Phi Phi Islands where she checks in to Zeavola Resort, a sustainable hotel she found through Green Pearls.
programme.sub-title: Ep 1 - Sustainability In Thailand | Zeavola Resort, Phi Phi Island

programme.title: Desert Architecture
programme.desc: Spanish Colonial Revival Architecture is an endless provider of independent outdoor livable spaces, and this special estate on the lower hillside of Camelback Mountain in Phoenix, Arizona is no exception. Also exceptional, the views: powerful canyon walls of Camelback on one 180 degrees panoramic side, and then the sunset view on the other, dramatized by downtown city lights creating an awe-inspiring foreground interspersed with mountains. The layout of this home is as unique as it gets to not miss a single framed view of both panoramas.
programme.sub-title: La Vida Dulce Estate - Phoenix, Arizona

programme.title: Ideas For Your Home
programme.desc: It's the holidays, and Sabine has a few tips to make this holiday season a bit smarter, healthier, and greener. She looks at LED Christmas lights, a new outdoor smart switch from iDevices to automate all those outdoor displays, and how to use clippings from around the landscape to create unique and beautiful wreaths and garlands for your home. She also looks at a few natural and healthy ways to bring that classic holiday fragrance into the home.

programme.title: Going Green Architecture & Design
programme.desc: The Eden Project in England holds the world's largest greenhouse! The project was set up to show its visitors the importance of saving the world's rainforests. In this video, we give you a tour of the indoor rainforest. The project is constructed using huge geodesic domes which hold two biomes. One holds the indoor rainforest and the other holds Mediterranean plants.
programme.sub-title: The Eden Project UK | The Largest Greenhouse In the World

programme.title: Going Green Architecture & Design
programme.desc:
What will the buildings of the future look like? We took a trip to the Futurebuild Exhibition in London to find out exactly what our homes, offices, and schools of the future could look like. Come check it out!
This exhibition aims to bring together a number of different sectors in the field of sustainability. From engineering to construction, architecture, and conservation, Futurebuild looks to inspire the transformational change that is needed to push the industry toward net-zero by showcasing some of the most innovative materials and technologies that are making a breakthrough today.
programme.sub-title: The Future of Architecture & Design | Futurebuild 2022

programme.title: Going Green Architecture & Design
programme.desc: These are the best green school examples from around the world. Each of the examples includes sustainable architecture using eco-friendly building materials. These schools provide children with environmental education and an understanding of how to be more sustainable and eco-friendly. This video features the Green School in Bali, the Copenhagen International School, and the Punahou school in Hawaii.
programme.sub-title: The Most Eco-Friendly Schools | Green Schools Around the World

programme.title: Hotels ByDesign
programme.desc: Journey through design-forward hospitality at Hotel Kansas City, explore wellness and art at Sensei Lanai, and embrace contemporary coastal elegance at Viceroy Santa Monica.

programme.title: Desert Architecture
programme.desc: Think modern architecture is stark, cold, better to look at than to live in? Think the desert is a hot barren inhospitable place best to be experienced in travel pictures from the Grand Canyon? Think again. Desert Wing is an award-winning home designed by architect Brent Kendle, AIA, LEED AP, that speaks poetically of its place in the world while demonstrating that even minimalist modern design can be comfortable and cozy.

programme.title: Desert Architecture
programme.desc: Situated on what most considered to be an unremarkable parcel of land compromised by both natural and municipal zoning limitations, architect Brent Kendle, AIA, LEED AP of Kendle Design Collaborative turned these limitations into advantages by flipping the traditional layout of the home on its head.

programme.title: The Travelling Chef
programme.desc: Brett visits the Kenyan coast and explores how the Swahili culture emerged and how it plays out in the food.

programme.title: Ideas For Your Home
programme.desc: It's the one room in the house that is truly the adult sanctuary and why not make it grand! From waterproof speakers in the shower, a luxurious bathtub, interesting vanity, and in-floor heating. The master bath at The Greenwich House has it all. Watch as Sabine takes you through her design choices for this relaxing and tranquil space.

programme.title: Desert Architecture
programme.desc: Situated on what most considered to be an unremarkable parcel of land compromised by both natural and municipal zoning limitations, architect Brent Kendle, AIA, LEED AP of Kendle Design Collaborative turned these limitations into advantages by flipping the traditional layout of the home on its head.

programme.title: Simple Dwelling
programme.desc: Winter Architecture was approached to design a renovation and extension to a two-bedroom Victorian home. Now providing four bedrooms and two bathrooms, the minimalist interior is filled with light from the courtyards, soft oak flooring and clean, crisp lines.
programme.sub-title: A Tired Victorian Home Turned Minimalist Interior

programme.title: Ideas For Your Home
programme.desc: Is your property ready for the winter? We have five tips for you to make sure your landscape and yard are healthy, strong, and ready for next season. We look at everything from mulching leaves, aerating your lawn, over-seeding, fertilizing with organic fertilizers, and creating a warm blanket for shrubs with the leaves that have fallen.

programme.title: Australia ByDesign: Architecture
programme.desc: Uncovering the stories behind some of Australia ’s finest architectural design s, we visit Bruny Island’s house at the end of the world, shine a spotlight on renowned Victorian Government Architect, Jill Garner, and discover Lisa McGuigan’s bold cellar door vision in Vamp.

programme.title: Desert Architecture
programme.desc: Have you ever wondered what it would be like to live in a modern home? A home where the line between inside and out is so blurred that nature sometimes comes crawling into your room. Are you afraid modern architecture is only for childless Avant guard art collectors who wear black turtleneck sweaters even in summer? Then take a moment to watch this Desert Wash video and see modern living through a child's eye. It will change your perspective about what site-sensitive modern architecture can be.

programme.title: Desert Architecture
programme.desc: The homeowners love to entertain. Every requirement was about enjoying the Arizona lifestyle while creating a resort-style environment. The architect used materials that are timeless and display well and are lasting. He visited the owners often and every time he did, they are deeply involved in a project such as making a grand meal, and I only see clients enjoying their home.

programme.title: Simple Dwelling
programme.desc: Melbourne architect, Jerry Wolveridge of Wolveridge Architects, bought the rural property of his clients, and after a study of local agricultural buildings, decided to design a simple, timber-clad pitched off-grid home. Jerry went a step further, adopting the construction methods of Australian sheds, using steel portal frames and avoiding typical "home" materials.
programme.sub-title: An Architect's Own Family Off-Grid Sustainable Home

programme.title: California ByDesign Innovations
programme.desc: In this new series of California By Design we’re on a quest to find best design innovations from around California. This episode features 6 Innovations including a hydrofoil surfboard, a machine that prepares the perfect baby bottle, and a look at what’s next from Uber.

programme.title: Desert Architecture
programme.desc: When I first visited this location, the opportunities presented by the incredible views were completely overwhelming. The site is located at the end of a cul-de-sac, on a golf course with good, natural privacy all around, and spectacular views of the distant, Continental Mountains.

programme.title: Desert Architecture
programme.desc: This Paradise Valley hillside home in the Sanctuary contains 6,080 sq. ft. of livable area. With 5,358 on the main level and an additional 732 sq. ft. on the lower level. Both the rocky hillside terrain and the pool are essential characteristics of the home. It embraces a modernist ideal. The complexity of a single-family house program can be abstracted and stripped to its essentials by using strictly rectangular/geometric forms.

programme.title: Rise: Sustainable Home Tours
programme.desc: Meet Melissa and Jim - they built their dream home a few years ago, but this wasn’t like any other home. Their main goal was to have a healthy home for their kids, and one that would also save on energy and environmental resources.
programme.sub-title: Leed Gold Minneapolis Lakefront Home Tour

programme.title: Rise: Sustainable Home Tours
programme.desc: Welcome to the Passive House Ranch! Homeowners Beate and Bern have created a state of the art modern home while preserving the structure's original character. Their passive house has a classic ranch design with high-performance features that bring next-level comfort.

programme.title: Rise: Sustainable Home Tours
programme.desc: Passive House is an easy to understand building standard that takes home energy efficiency to a whole new level using 5 building standards that are explained in this video.

programme.title: Rise: Sustainable Home Tours
programme.desc: Are you still using natural gas in your home? Have you thought about the health impacts of doing so? Bruce Nilles--a Senior Fellow at the Rocky Mountain Institute--realized that his biggest carbon footprint was his own home.
programme.sub-title: Why Electricity Is Better Than Natural Gas In Your Home

programme.title: California Architecture & Design
programme.desc: Richard & Alix were looking to remodel the home that they raised their children in, and didn't know where to start. Alix is a watercolor artist and had a painting that she wanted in incorporate into the design of the remodel.

programme.title: California Architecture & Design
programme.desc: This renovation of a single family home in the historic Venice Canals presented the opportunity to reimagine the house. The ground floor was reorganized to an open plan, allowing all rooms access to the view and outdoor spaces.
programme.sub-title: Carroll House by Dimster Architecture | Venice, California

programme.title: Ideas For Your Home
programme.desc: Sabine takes you through the design decisions for the kitchen at The Greenwich House. From a full-size island sink, making sure you get a durable farmhouse sink, cabinets that carry the weight, and energy-efficient appliances. She covers it all from top to bottom in this episode of Ideas For Your Home.

programme.title: Simple Dwelling
programme.desc: On a block measuring only 76m2 (818sqft), it was split in half with a pair of three-bedroom vertical townhouses, which meant they couldn't go 'out', so they went 'up'.
programme.sub-title: This Black Metal Townhouse Design is Inspired by a Handbag

programme.title: Ideas For Your Home
programme.desc: Your master closet doesn't have to be huge to be functional. The key is well-designed storage solutions that best utilize every inch you have. The storage solutions that Sabine worked into The Greenwich House are no exception. Watch as she takes you through her design choices to create one amazing "his and her" master closet.

programme.title: Hope and Health with Mathew Embry
programme.desc: Diagnosed with optic neuritis in 1994 and multiple sclerosis confirmed in 2002, Kelly Jubenvill has spent more than 30 years managing her health without medication. Guided by a science-based lifestyle focused on nutrition, exercise, and optimism, she’s learned to adapt through every stage of life from motherhood to post-menopause. In this episode of The Hope & Health Podcast, Mathew Embry talks with Kelly about discipline, mindset, and how choosing consistency over fear can help anyone create lasting wellness.
